summary: The meeting found that Mr. Lucas had misunderstood the architectural survey cost ceiling of $3,000.00, that invoices exceeded that figure by about $1,900.00, and resolved that the President and Secretary/Manager interview Mr. Lucas and seek agreement.
red_flag_reason: Architectural survey invoices exceeded the agreed $3,000 ceiling by about $1,900.
quote:
(ii) The President tabled a letter he had received from Mr. Lucas the
architect, together with invoices received by the Secretary/Manager
indicating that he had misunderstood instructions received regarding
the "ceiling" cost of the architectural survey.
The meeting reviewed the relevant correspondence and unanimously
agreed that the Secretary/Manager's letter of the 11th April, 1975
was quite clear and unequivocal in stating that the cost of the
survey was not to exceed $3,000.00.
In view of the fact that the invoices submitted exceeded this figure by
some $1900.00 three Trustees initially expressed the view that the
Trust should sever its connection with the firm of Fisher, Lucas
forthwith. However, after further discussion it was resolved that
the President and the Secretary/Manager should interview Mr. Lucas
and be empowered to reach an agreement with him.

summary: Because the School of Needlework said the patchwork quilt from Miss Wentworth's Bedroom was too delicate to repair, the meeting accepted Mrs. Kiernan's offer to attempt to preserve it with a covering of fine net.
red_flag_reason: The patchwork quilt was too delicate to repair, requiring preservation instead.
quote:
It was agreed, that in view of the information received from the
School of Needlework that the patchwork quilt from "Miss Wentworth's
Bedroom" was too delicate to repair, that Mrs. Kiernan's offer to
attempt to preserve it with a covering of fine net be gratefully
accepted.

summary: Because of inclement weather and soft ground, Mr. Ralph Clarke had not been able to complete trimming the Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room until the ground could support the 20-tonne crane.
red_flag_reason: Tree trimming was delayed because soft ground could not support the 20-tonne crane.
quote:
(i) Due to inclement weather and the resulting softness of the ground Mr.
Ralph Clarke has not been able to complete the trimming of the Moreton Bay
Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room. As soon as the ground is hard enough to
take the 20 tonne weight of the crane, he will finish the job.

summary: Storms during June resulted in the loss of five more trees and many broken branches, and grounds staff took almost a fortnight to complete clean-up.
red_flag_reason: Storms caused loss of five trees and broken branches, requiring almost a fortnight of clean-up.
quote:
(ii) Storms during the month resulted in the loss of five more trees and the
breaking of many branches. It took the grounds staff almost a fortnight
to effect a complete "clean-up".

summary: The Secretary/Manager advised Mr. Lucas not to proceed further with the architectural survey, and after the 2 June interview about his excessive account, the President was to report to the Board on 20 July 1975.
red_flag_reason: The survey was stopped because of an excessive account rendered for architectural services.
quote:
In accordance with your instructions at the last meeting I advised Mr. Lucas,
in writing, not to proceed any further with the survey. On the 2nd June
Mr. Lucas was interviewed by the President and the writer regarding the ex-
cessive account he had rendered for his services. The President will report
on this meeting to the Board on the 20th July, 1975.

summary: The June 1975 financial report stated that known committed expenditure required $1,418.66 more than was available in the Special Purposes Account because the Consultant Architect exceeded the architectural survey allocation, with July revenue expected to make up the projected deficit if no further commitments were made for one month.
red_flag_reason: Known committed expenditure exceeded the Special Purposes Account by $1,418.66 because the Consultant Architect exceeded the architectural survey allocation.
quote:
Therefore, the approximate amount required to enable the Trust to meet known
committed expenditure is $1418.66 in excess of what is currently available in
the Special Purposes Account. This situation is entirely due to the Consultant
Architect exceeding the amount allocated for the architectural survey. July
revenue should make up this projected deficit providing no further commitments
are entered into for a period of one month.

summary: The Alert Alarm Systems quotation for additions to the burglar alarm system was deferred pending reconsideration of Police Department recommendations.
red_flag_reason: A burglar alarm addition quotation was received, but no decision was made until Police Department recommendations were reconsidered.
quote:
(i) A quotation from Alert Alarm Systems for additions to the
burglar alarm system was received, but before making any decis-
ion it was agreed that Mr. Pierce and the Secretary/Manager
should re-consider the recommendations made by the Police
Department at the time the existing system was installed some
four years ago and if considered necessary contact the Police
Department for further recommendations.

summary: In principle, electro-osmosis systems were to be gradually installed in all walls subject to rising damp before re-decoration, following Drystat's discussion.
red_flag_reason: Rising damp in the walls was a continuing problem, and electro-osmosis systems were to be installed in affected walls before re-decoration.
quote:
(v) A letter from Drystat Pty. Ltd., written subsequent to a meeting
of the House Committee with their General Manager, Mr. D.J. van
Dommelen, to discuss the problem of rising damp in the walls was
considered. In view of the fact that a similar system had been
highly successful in controlling rising damp in Gilberthorpe's
Room it was agreed in principle that electro-osmosis systems
should gradually be installed in all walls subject to rising
damp, prior to re-decoration.

summary: The tea room lease remained unresolved because Mrs. Avenell could not proceed without Mr. Campbell, and the Vice-President and Legal Department agreed no more could be done at that time.
red_flag_reason: The tea room lease could not be finalised because Mrs. Avenell could not proceed without further consultation with Mr. Campbell, and both the Vice-President and Legal Department agreed no more could be done then.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager reported that in the continuing absence
through illness of Mr. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell
Catering Company he had interviewed Mrs. Avenell with a view
to finalising the terms of the lease for the tea room. Some
matters under query had been satisfactorily cleared up, but
with the few remaining, Mrs. Avenell felt that she could not
proceed without further consultation with her partner, Mr.
Campbell. She had promised to clarify the position as soon
as possible.

summary: Members expressed concern about the economic viability of the Tea Room lessees because of Mr. Campbell's illness, and the Secretary/Manager was to ask the bank manager to check M.A.C.C.'s financial soundness.
red_flag_reason: Members were concerned that Mr. Campbell's prolonged illness might affect the economic viability of the Tea Room lessees, and a bank enquiry into M.A.C.C.'s financial soundness was requested.
quote:
Discussion then reverted to the prolonged illness of Mr. Campbell
of M.A.C.C. and some members present expressed concern regarding
the effect of this on the economic viability of the lessees
of the Tea Rooms.

summary: The Trustees agreed that no restoration should be carried out in Gilberthorpe's Room until Mr. Lucas had inspected the exposed foundations and taken necessary photographs.
red_flag_reason: Restoration of the exposed foundations in Gilberthorpe's Room was withheld until Mr. Lucas inspected and photographed them.
quote:
The Trustees then examined the interior of the foundations
exposed by the removal of the floor boards and rotten joists
in Gilberthorpe's Room and agreed that no restoration should
be carried out until Mr. Lucas had carried out an inspection
and taken all necessary photographs.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room
summary: Mr. Ralph Clark's recommendations to trim the Moreton Bay Fig Tree were accepted, and the later report records that the $1,500 order for the work had been placed.
red_flag_reason: The tree was described as a considerable hazard and its complete safety could not be guaranteed.
quote:
<u>3. Trimming of Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room.</u>
Mr. Ralph Clark - the tree surgeon recommended by the Service
was in attendance and with the aid of photographs explained
what he considered was necessary to improve the health of this
tree and to make it considerably less of a hazard than it is
at the present time. He stressed that it was impossible for
anyone to guarantee complete safety of such a large and old
tree, but the treatment he was suggesting would, he considered,
extend the healthy life of the tree by approximately 100 years.
After some close questioning by the Vice-President and Mr.
Herford, it was agreed that Mr. Clark's recommendations should
be accepted and that the Executive should act upon his written
report and quotation for carrying out the work as soon as it
was received.

summary: The meeting deferred the Tea Room lease matter to the Legal Committee and Secretary/Manager, with an extraordinary meeting possible if contentious lease problems arose.
red_flag_reason: The Tea Room lease was unresolved because the Director's draft lease and the caterer's future proposals required legal action, and contentious lease problems could require an extraordinary meeting.
quote:
Two letters were tabled, one from the Director enclosing a
draft copy of the proposed lease and the other from Mr.
Campbell of Michael, Avenell Catering with supporting docu-
ments and plans showing what had been done in the Tea Room
since they took over its operation on the 18th October, 1975,
and proposals for the future with particular reference to
the establishment of a restaurant in addition to the Tea Room.

summary: The House Committee was to meet Mr. Lucas to discuss his unresolved kitchen restoration recommendations and matters arising from the architectural survey.
red_flag_reason: The architect's recommendations for the kitchen restoration and development were still unresolved and required further discussion.
quote:
Mr. Herford considered that Mr. Lucas - the architect, was
still "hedging" with his recommendations for the restoration
and development of the kitchen. After some discussion it
was agreed that the House Committee should meet Mr. Lucas
to discuss this matter and also question him regarding
matters arising from the interim report on the architectural
survey. The Secretary/Manager undertook to arrange a mutually
convenient date and time for this meeting.

asset: periphery of the park around the South Paddock
summary: The South Paddock clean-up and subsequent re-afforestation were deferred pending the result of the five-year-plan funding application.
red_flag_reason: The South Paddock clean-up and re-afforestation could not start until the result of the five-year-plan funding application was known.
quote:
Mr. Barrett reported that a number of large dead trees,
which were too big to be dealt with by our own staff,
would be felled by Mr. Lunney. General autu mn clearance
had started and would continue during the next three months.
The big clean up of the periphery of the park around the
South Paddock could not be started until we knew the result
of our application for funds for this work under the five
year plan. Likewise re-afforestation could not commence
until the clearing had been completed.

summary: The Legal, Insurance and P.R. Committee advised against hotel and travel-centre micro-film advertising and noted that $2,000 had been applied for in the 1975/76 budget for publicity.
red_flag_reason: Definite allocation of finance was needed to plan a proper publicity campaign, and the Treasurer advised that only $2,000 had been applied for in the 1975/76 budget.
quote:
Furthermore he considered that definite allocation of finance
was necessary to plan a proper publicity campaign. The
Treasurer advised that we had applied for $2,000.00 in the
1975/76 budget and expressed the opinion that our best re-
sults would be obtained by advertising in the appropriate
columns of the Sydney Morning Herald in conjunction with the
President's previous recommendation of taking space in
certain educational magazines.

summary: The President was to investigate whether the Trust could qualify for Australian Government restoration grants, while the Secretary/Manager doubted eligibility because the State Government owned Vaucluse House.
red_flag_reason: The Trust's eligibility for Australian Government restoration grants was doubtful because Vaucluse House was owned by the State Government.
quote:
A number of Trustees had recently noticed that quite consider-
able sums of money had been made available by the Australian
Government for restoration of historic buildings and wondered
if the Trust would be eligible for such a grant. The Secretary/
Manager said that as Vaucluse House was owned by the State
Government he was doubtful that we would qualify. However,
the President indicated that he would look into this matter.

summary: The executive would re-apply for replacement of the 14-year-old tractor, which was approaching the end of its economic life.
red_flag_reason: The tractor was 14 years old and approaching the end of its economic life, so replacement funding was being sought.
quote:
We will also re-apply for the replacement of the tractor
which is 14 years old and hence approaching the end of its economic
life.

summary: The Trust drew attention to the dangerous stump of the original Nielsen Park Pool concrete pile and agreed to have the appropriate service officer examine it; Sydney Bridge and Wharf could remove or make it safe when reinstalling the collapsed pile.
red_flag_reason: The original concrete pile stump was in a dangerous state and needed removal or making safe when the collapsed pile was reinstalled.
quote:
<u>(a) Nielsen Park Pool - collapsed pile</u>
The President drew the attention of the Trust to the danger-
ous state of the stump of the original concrete pile. It
was agreed that the appropriate service officer's attention
should be drawn to this matter. The Secretary/Manager
advised that Sydney Bridge and Wharf had indicated that
they could remove this or render it safe when they re-in-
stalled the collapsed pile.

summary: The Trust deferred a decision on kitchen roof repairs because the $3,256.62 quotation could not be met from current funds, and agreed to use the quotation as the basis for requesting special funds in the 1975/6 budget.
counterparty: A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters
red_flag_reason: The kitchen roof needed rusted nails replaced, flashings renewed and battens replaced, and the $3,256.62 quoted cost could not be met from currently available funds.
quote:
(4) Four quotations from A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters,
for various repair work to roofs were considered. It was
resolved to accept two, immediately covering repairs to
the roofs over the west wing and the gardener's cottage
in the total sum of $105. It was decided to defer the
making of a decision on the repairs to the kitchen roof,
as an examination had shown that all nails had rusted
away, flashings required renewal and some battens needed
replacement. This involved a quoted expenditure of
$3256.62 which could not be met out of currently available
funds. It was agreed that this quotation should form the
basis for the request of special funds from the Service
in the 1975/6 budget.

summary: The jury-rig supporting the Nielsen Park Pool nets was holding, and an arrangement had been made with Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. to drive a new pile later in the season or sooner if the rig failed; payment for the unsatisfactory pile was withheld.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. Pty. Ltd.
red_flag_reason: The pool pile was unsatisfactory and the supporting jury-rig was still needed, so payment for the pile was withheld while a new pile awaited installation.
quote:
<u>(c) Nielsen Park Pool - Collapsed Pile</u>
The Secretary/Manager amplified the remarks in his report for
December '74/January '75 and advised that the jury-rig erected by
the staff to support the nets was holding well and that he had
come to an arrangement with Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. Pty.
Ltd., to have a new pile driven either at the end of the swimming
season or sooner if the jury-rig collapsed at an earlier date.
Payment for the installation of the unsatisfactory pile has been
withheld.

asset: two-seater Victorian Toilet and old bricks
summary: The Trust agreed that the two-seater Victorian Toilet and old bricks should be put into safe storage until a more secure display position could be allocated.
red_flag_reason: The display items in the saddle-room were not securely displayed, so they needed safe storage pending a more secure display position.
quote:
(vii) A letter from the Secretary of the "Friends of Vaucluse House"
was read regarding the security of the two-seater Victorian Toilet
and old bricks presently displayed in the saddle-room of the
stables and also referring to the fact, already known to the Trustees,
that the guttering on the stables was not of 19th century design.
The Secretary/Manager then read notes he had made relating to the
points raised in the letter and as he would be proceeding on leave
the following day the President kindly offered to frame a suitable
reply.
It was further agreed that the toilets and bricks should be put
into safe storage pending the allocation of a more secure display
position.

summary: The Trust agreed to plant gum trees and other native flora around the South Paddock perimeter to replace dead trees when money became available for reconstituting that section of the Park.
red_flag_reason: Replacement planting of the South Paddock perimeter was postponed until money became available.
quote:
Mr. Barrett mentioned that consideration should be given to the
planting of gum trees and other native flora around the periphery
of the South Paddock to replace trees which had died over the
years. It was agreed that this should be done when money became
available for the reconstitution of this section of the Park.

summary: The Trustees viewed a further letter from Mr. Harris, Solicitor, requesting extracts from Trust Minutes as an impertinence and left it to the President to reply as he thought fit.
red_flag_reason: A solicitor's request for extracts from Trust Minutes was viewed as an impertinence and left unresolved pending the President's reply.
quote:
1. A further letter from Mr. Harris, Solicitor asking for
extracts from Trust Minutes was viewed as an impertinence.
It was left to the President to reply as he thought fit.

summary: The Treasurer reported that the Executive was satisfied with the caterers' operation of the Tea Room and had reached agreement in principle with Mr. N. Campbell on future glazing and restaurant toilets, but costs were not yet available and the Vice-President would meet Service Legal and the caterer's solicitor to clarify the lease points.
counterparty: Mr. N. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell Catering Company
red_flag_reason: Future glazing and toilet installation costs were not yet available, and the lease/licence terms needed further legal clarification.
quote:
On behalf of the Executive, the Treasurer then reported
on the meeting with Mr. N. Campbell - Manager of Michael
Avenell Catering Company. He said that the Executive
were more than satisfied with the manner in which the
caterers were operating the Tea Room and had reached agree-
ment in principle with Mr. Campbell relative to the future
glazing of the premises and the installation of the toilets
required for the proposed restaurant. Costs were not yet
available from the caterer's architect. Mr. Herford ex-
pressed the view that the caterers should be responsible for
insuring the new glazing when completed - it was agreed that
this should be noted for incorporation into the final lease.
The Treasurer further advised the meeting that Mr. Campbell
had accepted the Trust's recommendations and advice about
consulting Mr. K. Smithers when the time came to apply for
a win e licence for the new restaurant.

asset: kitchen chimney breast and windshield wall
summary: Further development of the kitchen was hampered by the lack of an architect's decision on the chimney breast and windshield wall, so the Secretary/Manager was instructed to arrange for Mr. Lucas to attend the next Trust meeting and present a progress report.
red_flag_reason: Further development of the kitchen was hampered by the lack of an architect's decision on the chimney breast and windshield wall.
quote:
(ii) Mr. Herford also commented that further development
of the kitchen was hampered by lack of a decision by our
architect relative to the chimney breast and windshield
wall. The President said that this was one of the points
he would raise in an interview he intended having with Mr.
Lucas before the next meeting. Apart from arranging such
a meeting, the Secretary/Manager was instructed to ask Mr.
Lucas to attend the next Trust meeting and present a pro-
gress report on work done.

asset: Moreton Bay fig tree, Kiosk and patio
summary: The Grounds Committee noted concern that branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree could fall on the Kiosk and patio, and agreed to engage a tree surgeon to examine the tree and quote for lopping where necessary.
counterparty: Mr. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell Catering Company
red_flag_reason: Concern was raised that branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree could fall on the Kiosk and patio.
quote:
the danger of branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree
falling on the Kiosk and the patio. It was agreed that we
should engage the services of a tree surgeon to examine
the tree and quote for "lopping" it where necessary.

summary: The meeting endorsed the Secretary/Manager's interim contact with Artstaff over an inaccurate advertisement for the Longhurst Drawings portfolio and decided that a clause requiring Trust approval of proposed advertising copy should be added to the agreement.
red_flag_reason: An inaccurate Sydney Morning Herald advertisement by Artstaff could expose the Trust to criticism, so advertising copy needed prior Trust approval.
quote:
A badly worded and inaccurate advertisement in the "Sydney
Morning Herald" inserted by Artstaff Pty. Ltd., offering copies
of the portfolio for sale, had been noted by Trustees. The
Secretary/Manager advised that he had, as an interim measure,
contacted Artstaff and asked that any future proposed advert-
isements should be submitted to the Trust for approval prior
to publication. The meeting agreed that Artstaff were en-
titled to attempt to dispose of the 1,000 copies of the
portfolio, which they had retained, by any legitimate means
but the advertising copy must not leave the Trust open to
criticism. The meeting endorsed the action taken by the
Secretary/Manager, but considered it imperative that a clause
be added to the agreement making it mandatory for Artstaff
to submit any proposed advertising copy, relating to the
drawings, for Trust approval. The Secretary/Manager under-
took to contact the Service Legal Department and have a suit-
able clause added to the agreement.

summary: The Secretary/Manager was given permission to pay the Nielsen Park Pool storm-damage account, provided Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited gave a firm written undertaking to make the pile installation good at the end of the swimming season or before pool closure if necessary.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited
red_flag_reason: The pile installation was unsatisfactory and the storm-damage account was being settled only on the condition that the contractor make it good later if necessary.
quote:
In view of the desirability of settling this "storm damage"
account as soon as possible, the Secretary/Manager was
given permission to pay this account providing Australian
Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited gave a firm written undertaking
to make it good at the end of the swimming season or at any
time prior to the closure of the pool should the necessity
arise. (Please see Secretary/Manager's current report).

summary: Preparatory work for repainting the drawing room outer walls was underway, but large areas of drumming plaster required re-rendering to help overcome rising damp, and final paint selection awaited consultation with Berger's Paints.
counterparty: Mr. Lucas; Technical Department of Berger's Paints
red_flag_reason: Large areas of drumming plaster and rising damp were affecting the drawing room outer walls.
quote:
(ii) Preparatory work for the repainting of the outer walls of the
drawing room is under way, but we ran into trouble with LARGE areas of
"drumming"plaster. After taking advice from our architect, Mr. Lucas,
some large areas are being re-rendered with a mixture which will allow the
walls to "breathe" thus helping to overcome the problem of rising damp.
A final decision on the type of paint to be used will be made after consul-
tation with the Technical Department of Berger's Paints.

summary: The Secretary/Manager discovered three more small areas of white ant activity, which were treated by Rentokil; the six-monthly inspection found no further activity but routine preventive measures were taken.
red_flag_reason: Three more small areas of white ant activity were discovered and had to be treated.
quote:
(ix) The writer discovered three more small areas of white ant activity
and these have been treated by Rentokil. Following this the six monthly
inspection taking three days was carried out. No further activity was dis-
covered, but routine preventive measures were taken.

summary: Despite prolonged dry weather, Mr. Kearney and his staff kept the gardens in good order with constant watering, but the south and west paddocks were in bad shape and two trees had crashed and been removed after high winds.
red_flag_reason: The south and west paddocks were in bad shape, and high winds had brought down broken branches and two crashed trees.
quote:
Despite the prolonged spell of dry weather Mr. Kearney and his staff
have kept the gardens in good order with constant watering, but the south
and west paddocks are in bad shape. High winds have on two occasions
littered the park with broken branches. Two trees have crashed and been
removed.

summary: Mr. Colin Green assumed control of Nielsen Park staff on 6 January 1975, but because he had no personal staff or facilities at Greycliffe House, the Secretary/Manager continued day-to-day administration; steps to legally invest Nielsen Park in the Director's care were likely to take at least another two months.
counterparty: Mr. Colin Green; Mr. George King
red_flag_reason: Legal investment of Nielsen Park in the Director's care was still pending, so the Trust remained legally responsible for Nielsen Park.
quote:
Officially the new Superintendent of Sydney Harbour National Park,
Mr. Colin Green assumed control over the staff of Nielsen Park on the
6th January, 1975, but at the same time Mr. George King - Assistant Director
had Mr. Green asked me to carry on with the day to day administration of
the two areas as Mr. Green at present has no personal staff or facilities
at Greycliffe House. This I agreed to do with the approval of the President.
I have established an excellent personal and working relationship with Mr.
Green and I know that our co-operation is greatly appreciated by the Service.

summary: The Service had money available to begin demolition of the damaged Nielsen Park jetty section, with officers to proceed after advising interested parties.
red_flag_reason: Damaged jetty section requires demolition and the work is still being coordinated with other parties.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that the Service had the money
available to commence demolition of the damaged section of
the jetty. Mr. Johnstone indicated that his officers in
the Operations Division had the matter in hand, and would
proceed with the work after advising other interested
parties, e.g. Maritime Services Board, Woollahra Council, etc.

summary: Mr. Lucas decided to proceed with accurate measured plans and drawings, but had not yet advised on the kitchen chimney breast and draught screen.
red_flag_reason: The architect had not given further advice on the kitchen chimney breast and draught screen, leaving the decision pending.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that Mr. Lucas did not con-
sider the copy drawings from the Mitchell Library were
very accurate and felt that he must, as originally planned,
proceed with the preparation of accurate, measured plans
and drawings.

summary: The trustees concurred with the President's handling of Mrs. Simpson's criticism, agreed to drop the correspondence, and asked for her 1972 report to be copied to House Committee members.
red_flag_reason: Mrs. Simpson's criticism of trustees' administration had generated correspondence with the Minister and required a decision to drop the matter.
quote:
The President again referred to the letter written by Mrs.
Simpson to the Minister and then read a letter which he
had written to her after discussing this matter at the
last meeting with the Trustees. He then read the reply
which he had received from Mrs. Simpson. The Trustees
concurred unanimously with the action taken by the President
and further agreed that no useful purpose would be served
by prolonging the correspondence and that therefore, the
matter should be dropped. It was however agreed that the
Secretary/Manager should provide the members of the House
Committee with a copy of Mrs. Simpson's original report
to the Trustees written in 1972.

summary: The trustees accepted the Brody Knight catering bill despite criticism, with trustees and counsellor paying for themselves and guests' meals and table and chair hire paid from the entertaining allocation.
red_flag_reason: Trustees were critical of the meal and service but had no alternative but to accept the bill as rendered.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager tabled a bill which had been rendered
by the Brody Knight Catering Service. All Trustees were
critical of the quality of the meal and the service provided,
but agreed that there was no alternative but to accept the
bill as rendered. It was agreed that all Trustees and the
Counsellor would personally pay for their wives and them-
selves, but that the guests' meals and the hire of the
tables and chairs would be paid from the special allocation
for entertaining. The Secretary/Manager was requested to
submit a bill to each Trustee and Counsellor.

summary: After receiving a conciliatory letter from Australian Bridge and Wharf about the Nielsen Pool pile, the trustees decided to continue withholding payment and arrange a meeting between company executives, Mr. Barrett and the Secretary/Manager.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.
red_flag_reason: The pile installation was unsatisfactory and payment was being withheld pending resolution.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager read a letter from the Managing
Director of the Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.
(formerly Sydney Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.) which was a
reply to his own letter expressing doubts as to the effic-
iency of the pile which had been driven in at the Nielsen
Pool. It was agreed that the letter from the Australian
Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd. was most conciliatory, but in the
circumstances a number of Trustees felt that we should
continue to withhold payment. Mr. Finlay confirmed that

summary: Despite local opposition, the trustees resolved to advise the Tea Rooms lessees to apply for the liquor licence and recommended engaging Mr. Ken Smithers for the hearing.
counterparty: Woollahra Council; Vaucluse House Protection Campaign; local residents
red_flag_reason: Local residents, the Vaucluse Progress Association, a protection campaign, Woollahra Council, and others opposed the proposed wine licence.
quote:
The Trustees received with satisfaction the letter from The
Minister of Lands signifying his approval for the Trustees
to support an application by the Lessee of the Tea Rooms
for a licence to serve wines and beer with a mid-day meal.
This application to be made in the normal manner through the
Licensing Court.

asset: kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen
summary: Mr. Herford pressed for a definite recommendation from Mr. Lucas on the kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen, and the Secretary/Manager undertook to apply pressure.
red_flag_reason: The architect had not given a definite recommendation for the kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen.
quote:
(iv) Insofar as re-constitution of the kitchen is concerned
Mr. Herford again stressed that pressure should be brought
to bear on Mr. Lucas, architect, to give a definite recommen-
dation on what should be done with the fireplace, chimney breast
and draught screen. The Secretary/Manager undertook to apply
as much pressure as possible.

summary: Mr. Doyle said revised insurance cover had not yet been finalised but would be dealt with as soon as possible, and the Trust agreed to proceed with a press-release public-relations suggestion.
red_flag_reason: Revised insurance cover had not been finalised because of pressures on Mr. Doyle's time.
quote:
Mr. Doyle said that many pressures on his time particularly
with regard to the proposed licence for the Tea Rooms had pre-
vented him finalising revised insurance cover, but he would
be dealing with this as soon as possible. Insofar as P.R.
was concerned he believed that a press release about four
times a year to the local papers relating to Trust activities
would be valuable in addition to any historical articles
submitted by Trustees. The Trust agreed that the committee
should proceed with this suggestion.

asset: kitchen fireplace and wind-break; gardeners' compound
summary: Further site discussions with Mr. Clive Lucas did not produce a firm recommendation on the kitchen fireplace and wind-break; he advised leaving the gardeners' compound as it was and screening with bushes or creeper.
red_flag_reason: Mr. Lucas remained unwilling to make a firm recommendation about the kitchen fireplace and wind-break.
quote:
(viii) As requested at the last meeting the writer has had further discussions
on site with Mr. Clive Lucas, but he is still unwilling to make any firm
recommendation regarding the kitchen fireplace and wind-break. Also, in
regard to the gardeners' compound, he considers that it should be left as

allow:-
